translationRepairs: Near the end of Zhao's reign the Xihe dependent chieftain Yijiuoru had mutinied with thousands; Fengshi had seized the staff and run him down.
Near the end of Emperor Zhao's reign the Xihe dependent chieftain Yijiuoru had mutinied with thousands; Fengshi had seized the staff and run him down.

Focus unit 昭帝末 names Emperor Zhao at the end of his reign; 'Zhao's reign' wrongly suggests the state of Zhao. Adding 'Emperor' restores the temple-name referent without changing the rest of the sentence.
Ren Qianqiu's father Ren Gong had served Zhao's chancellor as investigator, cut down mutineer Shangguan Jie, taken a marquisate, and ended as Grand Master of ceremonies under Xuan.
Ren Qianqiu's father Ren Gong had served Emperor Zhao's chancellor as investigator, cut down mutineer Shangguan Jie, taken a marquisate, and ended as Grand Master of ceremonies under Xuan.
Focus unit 昭帝時以丞相征事 places Ren Gong's service in Emperor Zhao's time as chancellor's investigator; 'Zhao's chancellor' misreads 昭帝 as the polity Zhao.
So Boyi was driven out, Mengzi the palace attendant was castrated, Crown Prince Sheng hanged himself, Qu Yuan drowned—the "Little Boy" ode and "Li sao" rose from such pain.
So Boqi was driven out, Mengzi was castrated, Crown Prince Sheng hanged himself, Qu Yuan drowned—the "Little Boy" ode and "Li sao" rose from such pain.
伯奇 is Boqi, not Boyi (伯夷), so the proposed name fix is right; but 孟子宮刑 marks the castration punishment and does not call Mengzi a palace attendant, so that invented office must also be removed.

Therefore Boyi was banished, Mengzi the Lu eunuch suffered castration, Sheng'er strangled with pheasant cord, Qu Yuan threw himself into the Xiang; the poem "Little Boy" was composed, the words of "Li sao" arose.

Therefore Boqi was banished, Mengzi suffered palace castration, Sheng'er strangled with pheasant cord, Qu Yuan threw himself into the Xiang; the poem "Little Boy" was composed, the words of "Li sao" arose.
Focus unit 伯奇 is Boqi, not Boyi; 孟子宮刑 states only that Mengzi suffered palace castration and does not identify him as a Lu eunuch. The proposed literal repairs both errors.
Shen was the Lady of Handsome Fairness's younger brother; his conduct was meticulous. His severity inspired fear, and he never drew near to serve within the curtained chambers.
Shen was the Brilliant Companion's younger brother; his conduct was meticulous. His severity inspired fear, and he never drew near to serve within the curtained chambers.
Focus unit 昭儀 is the consort rank Brilliant Companion; 'Lady of Handsome Fairness' is the usual English for 婕妤 and misnames the rank here, so the repair restores the correct title.

Shen was the younger brother of the Lady of Handsome Fairness; his conduct was moreover careful and complete. Because of his severity he was feared, and in the end he could not draw near to attend within the curtained chambers.

Shen was the younger brother of the Brilliant Companion; his conduct was moreover careful and complete. Because of his severity he was feared, and in the end he could not draw near to attend within the curtained chambers.
Same focus unit 昭儀; the literal must match the consort rank Brilliant Companion rather than the 婕妤 title 'Lady of Handsome Fairness'.
Let him bring Shen back to the capital to attend court at morning audience as a full marquis."
Let Shen return to the capital to attend court at morning audience as a full marquis."
Edict 其還參京師 is an imperative that Shen return to the capital; 'Let him bring Shen' invents a third-person agent the Chinese does not have.
Bring Shen back to the capital to attend court as a full marquis."
Let Shen return to the capital and attend court as a full marquis."
The idiomatic field retained the same invented agent as the corrected literal; 其還參京師 makes Shen the subject who is to return.
